author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Sixty Indonesian parents have filed a police complaint seeking a negligence investigation and compensation after their children became sick through the government’s free school-meal program, Reuters reported Friday. It is the first legal challenge reported against the flagship initiative.

The complaint concerns an outbreak in Karo, North Sumatra, where at least 300 students became ill in mid-August and some required hospital treatment. The filing was made August 31 and shared with news organizations on Thursday. Forensic testing of food connected to the incident is still pending.

Parents also plan a separate lawsuit in district court. The legal action increases pressure on authorities to explain how meals were prepared, transported and checked, and who may be responsible if investigators establish that safety failures caused the illnesses.

More than 50,000 food-poisoning cases have been linked to the nationwide program, according to figures cited by Reuters. The scale makes the complaint a potentially significant test of oversight and accountability. Investigators have not yet announced findings in the Karo case, and the requested compensation has not been awarded.
dek: Sixty parents are seeking a negligence investigation and compensation after hundreds of students became ill in North Sumatra.
headline: Indonesian parents file first legal challenge over free school meals
